notes:
• The chat follows new messages from the moment the world loads. Foundry follows a new message down only while the log is at its bottom, and it judges that from the log's scrolling. As a world loaded, Foundry drew the chat and scrolled it to its bottom; a moment later the HUD dressed the page as the device, every message grew a little, and the browser kept the view where it was, short of the new bottom. Foundry took that for the player having scrolled up, and from then on followed nothing until they scrolled down themselves. A player watching the chat scrolled without noticing; one who was in another window came back to find the chat stopped where it was. It happened on every load. The log is now kept at its bottom when it grows or shrinks under the player (the device's dressing, a font arriving late, a card redrawn), and when they come back to Foundry from another window, or to a tab that loaded while they were away. A log the player had scrolled up is left where they put it. In the sidebar and popped out; any world and any system. Checked in a Fallout 2d20 world: four loads out of four were stuck before, none after. Foundry 14.370 changed what it counts as the bottom of the log, from within a hundredth of its length to within twenty pixels; the HUD goes by Foundry's own mark, so it holds on both.
  • Speech bubbles hold all they say, and stay up long enough to read. Foundry sizes a bubble from a hidden copy of it in its own face, and the HUD draws the real one in the device's. Where the device's face is the wider one, as it is on the Pip-Boy, most of the sci-fi devices and the Journal's emotes, a line wrapped that the bubble had no room for, and was cut off. The copy is now measured in the face the bubble is drawn in, an emote in italics. Foundry kept a bubble up a fifth of a second a word, so a line of six words was gone in just over a second; it now stays two and a half seconds, and three tenths of a second more a word, up to Foundry's twenty. A long one scrolls through its words over that time, and a token that speaks again still replaces its bubble at once.

Full details in the release notes.
